newsitem.title: USA: Citizen Action sues US DOE on oil products reserve.
newsitem.headline: Citizen Action sues US DOE on oil products reserve.

text.p: The consumer watchdog group Citizen Action Wednesday said it filed a lawsuit to push the U.S. Energy Department to release documents on benefits and costs of establishing a regional petroleum products reserve.

"In light of DOE's history of opposition to a regional product reserve, which in part is in response to oil industry opposition, we believe it is necessary and in the public interest that any report, draft or otherwise, showing positive results be made public," Edwin Rothschild, Citizen Action's energy policy director, said in a statement.
The suit claiming that the Energy Department failed to comply with the Freedom of Information Act was filed in U.S. District Court here.

In the wake of last winter's spike in heating oil prices, some New England lawmakers are calling for a reserve of petroleum products on the idea it would help stabilize prices. Heating oil is used heavily in the Northeast.
The department is preparing a report on costs and benefits of such a reserve, which officials have said would be released this fall.

Rothschild said he believed "that there are DOE officials who do not want any part of this report to see the light of day. It is our understanding that the current draft has been sent to the Office of Management and Budget where some hope it will disappear."
But an Energy Department spokesman said the draft documents still were being reviewed within the department, and had not been sent to the OMB.
"So the data that Mr. Rothschild would like is considered pre-decisional" and exempt from the Freedom of Information Act, the spokesman said.
He also said the department solicited public comment on setting up a products reserve as part of a study it is doing on the Strategic Petroleum Reserve for crude oil.
"Not even Citizen Action responded to that. We received no responses from New England states, so we have not had an overwhelming response," he said.
